### What Is ISO Software for Merchant Cash Advance?


ISO software for merchant cash advance is a platform that ISOs and brokers use to run deals in one place. It captures merchant leads, collects documents, submits deals to many funders, tracks offers and commissions, and keeps compliance records.


An ISO, or Independent Sales Organization, is a company that sells financing on behalf of funders. A funder is the company that puts up the money. ISO software sits between the two and keeps every step of the deal moving.


This makes it different from the tools you may already use:


- **Generic CRMs:** These track contacts and emails, but they don't submit deals to funders or parse bank statements.
- **Lender loan origination systems (LOS):** These help a single lender approve its own loans. They can't shop one deal across many funders.
- **MCA ISO software:** This connects leads, documents, funders, commissions, and compliance in a single workflow.

### How MCA Financing and the ISO Model Work


A merchant cash advance (MCA) is a lump sum of cash a business gets today. The business pays it back with a share of its future sales, often through daily or weekly debits. It is not a traditional loan, so it has its own rules and pricing.


ISOs find merchants who need capital, gather their paperwork, and send their deals to funders. When a deal funds, the funder pays the ISO a commission. Many ISOs also earn on renewals, when a merchant takes a new advance after paying down the first one.


Demand for this product is real. The 2025[Fed Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/reports/survey/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms) of small employer firms found: "Reported separately, 26% of firms applied for a loan, 24% applied for a line of credit, and 8% applied for a merchant cash advance."


That mix matters for ISOs. Merchants often qualify for more than one product, so the best software lets you offer MCAs alongside term loans and lines of credit.

#### Lead Management and CRM


A merchant cash advance CRM tracks every merchant from first contact to funding. It should capture leads from web forms, landing pages, and partners. Then it should move each deal through clear pipeline stages.


Look for these lead tools:


- **Lead capture:** Pull leads from widgets, landing pages, and APIs into one queue.
- **Pipeline stages:** See which deals are new, submitted, approved, or funded at a glance.
- **Follow-up automation:** Send reminders so no merchant waits on a reply.
- **Renewal tracking:** Flag merchants who are close to paying off and may want a renewal.


For a deeper look at the CRM side, see this guide to choosing a[commercial loan broker CRM](https://www.lendflow.com/post/commercial-loan-broker-crm) .


#### Document Collection and Analysis


MCA funders want to see bank statements, an application, and often ID and tax records. Bank statement analysis is the review of those statements to check revenue, deposits, and existing debts. Done by hand, it can take hours per deal.


Skip the manual review—use[automated document analysis](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/doc-analyzer) to read files and pull key data. Lendflow's Doc Analyzer extracts the numbers funders need, so your team spends less time on paperwork.


#### Funder Integrations and Submission Portals


A funder submission portal lets you send one deal package to many funders at once. Instead of emailing each funder, you submit once and track offers as they come back.


Lendflow's Data Orchestration connects you with top integration partners in minutes. It also builds decline waterfalls. A decline waterfall is a set of rules that sends a declined deal to the next funder or product. That way, no deal is leaving money on the table.


This is where multi-product support pays off. An MCA turndown can route to an invoice factoring, equipment financing, or SBA loan offer instead. Pre-qualified offers hosted on Lendflow drive an average of 42% faster speed to funding.


Your funder list matters as much as your software. Learn more about[building a funder network](https://www.lendflow.com/post/building-the-right-lender-network-why-it-matters-for-business-loan-brokers) that fits your merchants.


#### Commission Tracking and Reporting


ISO commission tracking shows what you earned on each deal and from each funder. Without it, payouts get missed and disputes drag on.


Good MCA reporting goes beyond commissions:


- **Earnings by funder:** See which funders pay best and fastest.
- **Conversion rates:** Track how many leads turn into funded deals.
- **Renewal pipeline:** Spot upcoming renewals before a competitor does.

### Compliance and Transparency Requirements for MCA ISOs


Rules for MCA brokers vary by state, and several states have added new ones in recent years. MCA compliance software helps by storing disclosures, timestamps, and messages in one audit trail.


This section is for general education only and is not legal advice. Talk to a qualified attorney about the rules that apply to your business.


#### State Disclosure and Licensing Rules


A commercial financing disclosure is a form that shows the merchant the cost and terms of an offer. In New York, these rules cover commercial financing deals of $2.5 million or less. The[NY DFS disclosure regulation](https://www.dfs.ny.gov/industry_guidance/regulations/final_financial_services/rf_finservices_23nycrr600_text) states that "a broker shall transmit the unaltered disclosures received from the financer to the recipient."


California is adding licensing. AB 2116 was signed on September 30, 2026. The[California AB 2116 bill status](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billStatusClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB2116) reads "Chaptered by Secretary of State - Chapter 823, Statutes of 2026."


Under AB 2116, licensing for covered providers and brokers on California deals of $500,000 or less begins in 2028. ISOs serving California merchants should plan now.


At the federal level, the[CFPB Section 1071 rulemaking](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/1071-rule/) sets small business lending data rules, with compliance "extended to January 1, 2028." Ask counsel whether your products fall in scope.


#### Fee Transparency and Merchant Trust


Cost surprises hurt trust across small business finance. The Fed's[2026 Report on Employer Firms](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/reports/survey/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms) found: "Sixty percent of those that borrowed from online lenders reported that actual borrowing costs were higher than expected." That figure covers online lenders broadly, not MCAs alone.


Clear status updates help prevent those surprises. A[branded borrower portal](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/borrower-platform) gives merchants one place to upload files, see offers, and track their deal.


Regulators also act when fees aren't clear. In a 2021 federal case, the[FTC Yellowstone settlement](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2021/04/cash-advance-firm-pay-98m-settle-ftc-complaint-it-overcharged-small-businesses) announced that Yellowstone Capital "will pay more than $9.8 million to settle Federal Trade Commission charges."

### How to Choose the Right ISO Software for Your MCA Business


The best MCA ISO software fits your deal volume today and your growth plans for next year. Start with your biggest bottleneck, then check each platform against the list below.


Use this checklist when you compare platforms:


- **Deal volume:** Can it handle your monthly submissions without slowing down?
- **Funder coverage:** Does it connect to the funders you use now and the ones you want next?
- **Multi-product support:** Can a declined MCA route to term loans, lines of credit, or factoring?
- **Document automation:** Does it read bank statements, or just store them?
- **Compliance records:** Does it save disclosures and messages with timestamps?
- **Reporting:** Can you track commissions, conversion rates, and renewals in one dashboard?
- **Implementation speed:** Can you go live in days with widgets, landing pages, and APIs?
- **Pricing:** Is the cost clear, and does it scale with your volume?

### FAQ


#### What is an ISO in merchant services?


An ISO, or Independent Sales Organization, is a company that sells financial products like merchant cash advances on behalf of funders or banks. In finance, ISOs find merchants, prepare their deals, and earn a commission when deals fund.


#### How do ISOs earn commissions on merchant cash advances?


The funder pays the ISO a commission when a deal funds, often set as a share of the advance amount. Many ISOs also earn commissions when merchants renew.


#### What is the difference between an ISO and a direct funder?


A direct funder provides the money and sets the terms of the advance. An ISO connects merchants to one or more funders and does not fund the deal itself.


#### How does ISO software integrate with MCA funders?


ISO software connects to funders through APIs or submission portals, so one deal package reaches many funders at once. Platforms like Lendflow also use decline waterfalls to route turndowns to the next funder or product.


#### How does ISO software help with MCA compliance?


It stores disclosures, messages, and timestamps in one audit trail, so you can show what each merchant received and when. That record helps you meet state rules like New York's broker disclosure duty.
